rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran. 10 blocking findings remain, 3 of them decision_needed: CR-004, the 3-attempt cap that drops an unsent end metric after three daemon starts; CR-006, at-least-once end-metric sends; and CR-009, the attribution rewrite with no security sign-off. Several are graded at most major because reachability was unconfirmed. 0 deferred; 17 candidates dismissed as noise, already guarded, or below the floor, including the PascalCase file names and missing JSDoc.

standards_review.notes: 1 subject in range (fix(proxy): ...) uses an allowed type and scope from git-workflow.md, imperative mood, 85 chars total (under the 100-char subject limit)

Most of code-quality.md is met: imports end in .js, no console.log, no generic Error (new ReconcileLockHeldError extends CodeMieError), new methods under 50 lines, new files under 500 lines, exported return types explicit. Unmet: the 'Files: kebab-case.ts' rule, because new files src/telemetry/runtime/DesktopSessionDelivery.ts and DesktopSessionMetrics.ts are PascalCase (the folder's existing DesktopTelemetryRuntime.ts and DesktopRepositoryResolver.ts already do this). Also unmet: the 'JSDoc on all public APIs' rule, because exported isSameFingerprint and RecordKind in src/telemetry/runtime/desktop-session.ts have no JSDoc

No hardcoded secrets. Credential loading moved unchanged into DesktopSessionMetrics.ts, and only the URL and error message are logged. Unmet: security-practices.md 'CRITICAL: Project & User Attribution Headers' rules 1-2. DesktopTelemetryRuntime.retrackSession (src/telemetry/runtime/DesktopTelemetryRuntime.ts:371-386) adds a new path that rewrites an existing session's gitBranch, repository and project from a newly discovered working directory. The END metric and later deltas then carry these values. The range shows no recorded security-review sign-off. The same block also logs from/to working-directory paths and the repository at info level, without sanitizeLogArgs

findings.title: Pre-upgrade daemon without /health pid read dead
findings.problem: answersOnOwnPort requires body.pid === pid, but only the new proxy reports pid in /health. A live daemon started before this change that fails the one-sided start check (forward wall-clock step > 60 s) is read as gone.
findings.impact: checkStatus/stopDaemon clear its state without signalling it and ensureOtlpProxy/spawnDaemon start a second daemon while the old one still holds the port, leaving an orphan. Reachability unconfirmed: it needs an upgrade-time daemon plus a forward clock step.
findings.recommendation: Accept a /health body with no pid as a match on port alone (body.pid === undefined || body.pid === pid), or treat a live pid with a failed start check and a pid-less /health as alive; add a test for a pre-upgrade body.

findings.title: Health timeout clears a live daemon's state
findings.problem: checkStatus and stopDaemon delete the state file whenever isDaemonAlive is false. That includes a live pid that failed the start check and whose /health only timed out (1.5 s shallow deadline) or answered non-ok while busy or restarting. No 'unknown' outcome keeps the state.
findings.impact: A temporary slowdown orphans a running daemon: stopDaemon sends no signal, the next spawn collides on the port. Reachability unconfirmed: it requires a failed start check first.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish 'gone' from 'unknown': when the pid is alive but the start check failed and /health errored or timed out, keep the state (checkStatus) and still signal or refuse (stopDaemon) instead of clearing state without signalling.

findings.title: Real /health pid field is untested
findings.problem: Regression gap: no test checks that the real CodeMieProxy /health body includes pid. daemon-manager tests stub fetch with bodies that carry the pid themselves; connect-orchestrator tests mock fetchProxyHealth to reject; the only real /health request (transparent-vscode-proxy.integration.test.ts:260-269) asserts only status 200.
findings.impact: Consumer: isDaemonAlive -> answersOnOwnPort (daemon-manager.ts), used by checkStatus, spawnDaemon, stopDaemon and ensureOtlpProxy. Dropping or renaming pid would make a live daemon that fails its start check read as dead (state cleared, second daemon spawned) while every test stays green.
findings.recommendation: In transparent-vscode-proxy.integration.test.ts 'keeps health unauthenticated', assert the started proxy's /health body toMatchObject({ status: 'ok', port: <actualPort>, pid: process.pid }); or run isDaemonAlive against a real CodeMieProxy with isOwnerAlive forced false.

findings.title: End metric dropped after three daemon starts
findings.problem: EPMCDME-16545 is only partly met. deliverLocked counts one attempt per finalize and per daemon start, and at MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) it saves the record, marks it droppedAt and renames it completed_* without sending. The PR spec caps start-time re-delivery at 3, but the ticket says a failed end metric is delivered again on the daemon's next start.
findings.impact: If the outage lasts through about three daemon starts (stop/start cycles, which CR-007 also burns), the end metric is lost for good and the session shows as dropped, which the ticket's expected result rules out.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the 3-attempt cap applies to Desktop end metrics. If the ticket's 'delivered again on the next start' wins, stop counting start-time attempts for undelivered Desktop records (or cap only sync, never the end metric) and keep the record live until the end metric is sent.

findings.title: No-SSO records never count as delivered
findings.problem: When there are no SSO cookies, sendSessionEndMetric returns without setting endMetricSentAt or endMetricSkipped. renameToCompleted is now gated on isDeliveryDone, so for a non-SSO provider (e.g. litellm; the daemon builds the runtime for any provider in claude-desktop mode) the record is never done.
findings.impact: Every daemon start spends an attempt, and after 3 the record is renamed with droppedAt and reported as 'dropped' in analytics, even though no send was ever possible. Reachability unconfirmed: whether claude-desktop telemetry runs with non-SSO providers in practice was not established.
findings.recommendation: When the provider has no SSO credentials by design (non-SSO provider), set endMetricSkipped so isDeliveryDone holds and the record is renamed without a droppedAt mark; keep the retry only for an SSO provider whose credentials are temporarily missing.

findings.title: End metric can be sent twice
findings.problem: EPMCDME-16545 'sent once' is only partly met. endMetricSentAt is saved only after sendSessionEnd resolves. The code's own ponytail comment admits that a process cut between the server's 200 and this save sends the end metric again on the next delivery.
findings.impact: A daemon killed at that point (for example the SIGKILL 5 s into stopDaemon) produces a duplicate session-end metric, which double-counts the session in analytics.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether at-least-once is acceptable against the ticket's 'sent once'. If not, send an idempotency key (e.g. session id + stretch start) the backend dedupes on, or mark the send as in-flight before the request and reconcile on restart.

findings.title: Daemon stop spends delivery attempts
findings.problem: stop() neither awaits nor cancels startupPass/redeliveryPass, then finalizes each tracked session one after another (lock wait, flush, sync, end metric with a 10 s timeout and retries). stopDaemon sends SIGKILL after 5 s. deliverLocked saves deliveryAttempts+1 before any send.
findings.impact: A stop that is killed partway leaves attempts counted for sends that never completed, and an in-flight pass may hold the lock the stop-time finalize waits on. Together with the 3-attempt cap (CR-004), this pushes records toward being dropped unsent.
findings.recommendation: In stop(), await Promise.allSettled([this.startupPass, this.redeliveryPass]) before finalizing, and bound stop-time finalization (or skip counting the attempt) so a SIGKILL after 5 s does not consume one of the three delivery attempts for a send that never completed.

findings.title: Transcript switch keeps old sync index
findings.problem: On a folder switch, retrackSession points correlation.agentSessionFile at the new transcript but keeps sync.conversations.lastSyncedHistoryIndex and the tracked fingerprint from the old file. Analytics (recordTranscriptPath, cost enricher) also resolve only the new transcript. The test covers only a copy with the same message count.
findings.impact: If the new folder's transcript is not a full copy of the old one, conversation messages are skipped or sent twice, and tokens recorded only in the old transcript are left out of pricing. Reachability unconfirmed: depends on how Desktop writes the switched transcript.
findings.recommendation: When agentSessionFile changes, reset or re-derive sync.conversations.lastSyncedHistoryIndex and the transcript fingerprint against the new file unless it is verified to be a superset copy; cover a new transcript with a different message count in a test, and confirm analytics pricing covers pre-switch tokens.

findings.title: Attribution rewrite lacks security-review sign-off
findings.problem: security-practices.md (the CRITICAL attribution section, rules 1-2) requires security-review sign-off before attribution identifiers are rewritten or derived from a new source. retrackSession overwrites a live session's gitBranch, repository and project from a newly discovered working directory, and the range records no sign-off. The same block logs raw from/to working-directory paths and the repository at info level without sanitizeLogArgs.
findings.impact: Blocks the workflow under the project's security policy. A silent re-attribution can attribute analytics to the wrong repository, and raw paths reach info-level logs.
findings.recommendation: Record security-review sign-off and mark the change CRITICAL in the PR description (or keep the original attribution on folder switch); pass the folder-switch log fields through sanitizeLogArgs or log them at debug.

findings.title: Folder switch may never re-attribute session
findings.problem: EPMCDME-16248 'attributed to the folder where the work happened' is only partly met. retrackSession re-detects branch, repository and project only when discovered.workingDirectory changes. The unchanged discovery (claude-desktop.discovery.ts:202-209) builds that value from companion/metadata originCwd first, and the ticket names originCwd as folder A, which stays the same after the switch. The unit test sets the discovered workingDirectory by hand.
findings.impact: In the ticket's scenario the folder-switch branch may never fire, so the session stays attributed to folder A while the work happens in folder B. Reachability unconfirmed: whether Desktop updates originCwd on a switch was not established, so graded major.
findings.recommendation: Trigger re-attribution from a signal that actually changes on a Desktop folder switch (e.g. the transcript's directory/cwd or userSelectedFolders), not discovered.workingDirectory built from originCwd first; add a test that goes through claude-desktop.discovery with a switched-folder fixture.
